Actually, I believe it's far more interesting than that.

We live in a world where the classic models of fascism and oligarchy not longer work, at least from a first world perspective, and all of this for very simple reasons: capitals flow freely between borders. We have seen this happening for decades: huge agreements made to destroy barriers for capital, never people... in fact, it could be said that new barriers have been build to keep people in their respective socioeconomic situation.

Anyway, on traditional oligarchy "models" a ruling party, consisting of those of economic power, is "trapped" by the frontiers of their own country. Their capital and power are chained to their geographic position by barriers naturally imposed by other countries. Trying to "flee" a country would normally mean a massive destruction of their assets and with them, their power.

However, without these barriers it's possible for the capital to move from one place to another, or worse, the capital could become bound only to the individual/group, never to a country.

So what happens then? For starters, without the capability to effectively secure big money in its borders, the country loses a lot of its economic and even sovereign powers. In fact, as we have seen countless times in the past, to "invite" this capital to come or even just stay, the countries frequently have to compromise their own environmental, tax and work regulations to please this external money... What happens if they fail to do so? The capital moves to the next country willing to offer it everything it wants. In other words, less work, taxes... poverty. (This is not new, third world countries are used to this)

So what the hell this has to do with the USA & Europe, welp, it seems that big money is finally realizing that big old first world is not enough for their "needs" and they have the power to change this. All those annoying regulations that make making obscene amounts of money difficult have to disappear... how they do this? The same way the do it with third world countries: if the want jobs, they have to obey.

Naturally there is an interesting problem left for the "free capital": first world countries are still their money makers (consumers), they can't simply "get rid" of them and wait for the emerging markets to replace them. While at this point I don't know how they plan to address this, I believe their solution is somewhere around weakening the strong countries while empowering weak ones in way that maximizes the profits... or find a way to profit from the poor.

Please don't think this is a big conspiracy organized by some shady powerful figures... this stuff is the natural consequence of uncontrolled capitalism and the technological advances in transportation and telecommunications. Hell, for those who think a centralized world government could be born from this, you are wrong! The last thing free capital wants is something that could regulate it... in fact, weak countries are its favorite thing!
